name: Wat
look: A stocky, bow-legged carter in his fifties with a ruddy face, a battered wide-brimmed hat, a mud-caked smock, gaiters, and a long whip over his shoulder.
personality: Loud, cheerful and stubborn; swears at the mud and the ox in turn, and is pathetically grateful to anyone who helps.
values: his cart, his ox, getting the cider to the inn on time
fears: losing the load, the inn's anger
authority: Owns the cart, the load and the ox.

relations.npc_rook_boy: Rook, the boy from the farm

concerns: The cart's sunk to the axles in the mire with four barrels of cider aboard. Bess the ox can't shift it alone and he's pushed till he's blue.

load.text: The cart has four barrels of cider aboard, a good weight.
load.line: Four barrels of cider on her. That's the trouble: too heavy for the mud.
load.lead: Wat's cart carries four heavy barrels of cider.

help.text: Dunna's strong as an ox herself, and the boy Rook will lend a hand for a penny.
help.line: Dunna there could lift the cart on her own, near enough. And the lad'll help if you ask.
help.lead: Dunna and the boy Rook might lend a hand with Wat's cart.

persuaded_by: anyone who'll put their back into it
style: Loud and cheerful, with mild oaths.

samples: If you've a better notion, I'm all ears.
You've earned a barrel, friend. Well. A cup.
voice.habits: Mutters at the ox; kicks the wheel; thumbs his hat back.
voice.greeting: Wipes his brow: 'Don't suppose you've a strong back?'

goals: Get the cart out of the mire
Get the cider to the inn
dislikes: mud, the parish for not mending the lane

npc_dunna_farmer.text: a good neighbour, strong as two men

superstition.text: Wat would want to know how it works.
